problemSolution: Millions of girls and women in Nigeria lack access to affordable menstrual products, adequate menstrual health education, and safe sanitation facilities. Period poverty contributes to school absenteeism, poor health outcomes, gender inequality, and reduced economic participation. Hygiene Heroes addresses these challenges by manufacturing affordable, high-quality reusable menstrual pads that last up to 24 months, while delivering menstrual health education through community outreach, schools, and an AI-powered multilingual chatbot. Our integrated solution improves menstrual health, reduces plastic waste from disposable sanitary products, empowers girls to stay in school, and promotes dignity, health, and economic inclusion for women and girls across Africa.
tractionEvidence: ygiene Heroes has directly impacted over 1,000 girls and women across Lagos, Abuja, Ibadan, Port Harcourt, and Akwa Ibom through menstrual health education, reusable menstrual pad distribution, and advocacy programs. Hygiene Heroes emerged as a First Prize Winner at Global Tech Africa (Victoria Island, Lagos) and has secured land for the establishment of a reusable sanitary pad manufacturing facility. We continue to receive strong interest from development partners, investors, and organizations working to advance gender equality and women's health.

Certain ingredients in skin care products have been found to be detrimental to human health, some are carcinogenic, cause disruption of hormones, infertility, and a host of other health issues.

In August 2018, I was down with a breast crisis thought to be a result of the accumulated use of toxic chemical-based skincare products. In addition, I was also battling chronic acne that maimed my confidence and my dream of being a face model. I was stigmatised by my peers and became depressed. I tried several prescriptions which never worked but rather aggravated my skin condition.
In the quest to stay healthy and alive, I decided to go all natural, including my hair.

I started experimenting with natural ingredients in my kitchen, and found what eventually worked for my acne-prone skin, and that was how ZeeNature was born. Formulating clean beauty products free from harsh and toxic ingredients.

Generalised and a lack of user-specific skincare products result in trial and error that can cause skin damage.
Through our consultation channel and skin Ai, we offer user-specific skincare products that prevent skin damage in hyper-allergic and sensitive skin, which most brands can not adequately cater for, as over 80% of the total population in Africa experiences sensitive skin.

Using our unique line of products, customers do not have to worry if recommended products will work for them, tamper with their complexion, or cause irritations and reactions.

Our product model is lifestyle-influenced and integrated at every stage of our customers' lifecycle for adults and children.

Zeenature are high quality skincare products for inner health and beauty; produced from natural base ingredients home to the continent of Africa. These ingredients are mainly agricultural produce like tiger nut, walnut, carrot, cucumber, aloe vera, coconut, herbs, fruits, flowers, oils, dairy products, and more. Varieties of products are formulated to suit specific skin types and thoroughly treat skin problems like acne, sunburn, hyperpigmentation, stretch marks, eczema, and more.

• Treatment soaps and creams
• Moisturizers
• Facial care such as toners, serums, facial masks, face creams, scrubs

Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are the backbone of Nigeria's economy, with over 39.6 million MSMEs contributing significantly to employment and economic growth. 
In Edo State, the rapid growth of small businesses, social commerce, and online vendors has increased demand for affordable, reliable, and efficient last-mile logistics services.
The increase in fuel prices, from approximately ₦700 to over ₦1,700 per litre in the last 18 months, has driven average local delivery costs from about ₦1500 to as much as ₦4000 per trip. This leads to reduced profit margins, discourages customer purchases, and limits their ability to expand beyond their immediate communities.
As a result, over 40% of SMEs struggle to access affordable delivery, reach new customers, and compete effectively in the growing digital economy. This challenge is particularly pronounced for micro-enterprises, restaurants, pharmacies, grocery stores, and social media vendors that rely on timely and cost-effective delivery to sustain their businesses.
Zummey, a clean-tech decentralised logistics service based in Benin City, addresses this challenge by connecting businesses to customers using vehicles independent of inflation, that is, electric vehicles, and also an online tracking and matching platform. 
We offer a swift, insurance-backed, trackable delivery at a rate 30% less than traditional logistics. What this means for a local vendor on Sapele Road is a 1000 naira or a 1500 cutback, depending on the distance for every delivery. In the long run, the economic backbone of Edo State- local traders, small businesses, and vendors expand their customer base, fulfil orders more efficiently, improve customer satisfaction, and increase sales.
While we keep the trading activity alive in Edo State, we are covering the gap of youth employment by providing sustainable jobs: Vetted riders and internship opportunities in tech. We have increased the financial independence of 50 youth in Edo State and provided 2 paid internship opportunities in tech. By addressing one of the barriers to business growth and reducing unemployment amongst youth in Edo State, we are building a resilient and sustainable digital economy in Edo State.

Africans travelling within Africa lose up to $3.75 billion annually to FX fees and broken cross-border rails that were never built for them.
Spending money outside of Nigeria is one of the most stressful things travelers/tourists have to face. A Nigerian travelling to Kenya still has to visit the black market bureau or carry physical Dollar before he can transact in Nairobi, not to mention the stress involved in getting a local bank account. Most payments made in African tourist countries are routed through Europe or the United States before settling locally. That is $5 billion being lost annually to non-African GDP 

60 percent of all tourism spending in Africa comes from Africans travelling within the continent. That is a $15 billion annual market where travelers lose up to 25 percent of every transaction to FX fees, middlemen, and broken payment rails.

Chainpaye solves all of this from WhatsApp without the need to download any app. Users deposit naira, stablecoin or USD convert at live rates, and send local currency to any bank account across 8 African countries in under 60 seconds.

The Problem
When I launched this venture, I realized we were facing two distinct, major challenges in the market:
• The Awareness Gap & Low Market Demand: The baobab fruit is an absolute powerhouse of nutrition and skincare benefits, but the general public simply didn't know it. When we operated under a traditional business-to-business (B2B) model, we struggled to generate pull-through demand because consumers weren't actively looking for baobab products on standard retail shelves.
• The Economic & Skills Gap for Women: In communities like mine in Ebonyi State, there is a massive, untapped potential of women who lack access to structured manufacturing skills, sustainable micro-enterprise opportunities, and premium health products that truly care for their well-being.
The Solution
To solve these problems, I completely re-engineered our business model from the ground up:
• A Community-Driven MLM Model: Instead of waiting for retail customers to discover us, I shifted our commercial framework to a Multi-Level Marketing (MLM) structure. By doing this, we don't just sell products; we build a network of passionate health and business enthusiasts. They act as educated advocates, raising public awareness through direct relationships and grassroots education, which effectively drives product demand and rewards our community financially.
• A Premium, Diversified Product Line: We transform raw baobab into high-value, market-ready consumer goods under the Lentoc brand. We handle the technical commercial food processing (creating nutrient-dense food formulations) and cosmetics manufacturing (creating premium skincare) to capture both the wellness and beauty markets.
• Empowerment Through Initiatives Like "Healthy Women, Beautiful Ebonyi": We directly bridge the skills gap by using our manufacturing processes as a tool for social impact. Through targeted training and empowerment programs, we equip local women with the exact skills needed to produce and distribute these products, turning them into self-reliant micro-entrepreneurs.
• Uncompromising Quality & Compliance: To give our network and consumers absolute confidence, we ensure every product is backed by rigorous operational standards. We are actively locking down our standard operating procedures (SOPs) and securing strict regulatory compliance through NAFDAC to guarantee that what we produce is safe, premium, and globally competitive.

How will you use the ₦10M grant?

Welup Digital will deploy the ₦10,000,000 grant across two strategic priorities designed to reduce operational costs, increase student capacity, and accelerate growth in Edo State and the broader South-South region.

1. Learning Management System (LMS) Development: ₦6,500,000 (65%)
The single largest operational constraint limiting Welup Digital's ability to scale is the absence of a proprietary Learning Management System. Currently, delivering training at volume requires significant human resource overhead, manual coordination across multiple tools, and recurring costs that compress margins and limit how many students we can serve simultaneously.

Building a dedicated LMS solves this structurally. The platform will centralise course delivery, student progress tracking, assessments, mentor communication, certification issuance, and job placement coordination in one system. Once built, the cost of adding each additional student drops significantly, making it possible to serve Edo State's youth at scale without a proportional increase in operational expenditure.

The LMS will be built with the following capabilities:
Self-paced and cohort-based course delivery across all existing Welup skill tracks. Automated progress tracking, assessment, and certification. Employer portal for direct graduate recruitment. Scholarship and bursary management module for tracking and administering access funds. Analytics dashboard for real-time program performance monitoring and impact reporting.

2. Marketing and Student Acquisition: ₦2,500,000 (25%)
With the LMS infrastructure in place, the second priority is demand generation, specifically targeted at Edo State and the South-South region. This allocation funds a structured marketing campaign to recruit students into the first Welup Edo cohort, build brand awareness within the state, and establish Welup Digital as the leading digital skills training provider for Edo's youth.
Channels will include targeted digital advertising, community-based outreach partnerships with existing Edo institutions and youth organisations, and a referral program leveraging the 142 Edo students already trained through our programs.

3. Operations and Program Management: ₦1,000,000 (10%)
This covers program coordination, impact documentation, reporting obligations to EYIF, and the administrative infrastructure required to manage a grant-funded cohort responsibly and transparently.

This allocation is designed to produce two outcomes simultaneously: a technology asset that permanently reduces Welup Digital's cost-to-serve and an Edo State student base that demonstrates the platform's capacity to deliver impact at scale. The LMS does not just serve this grant cycle. It serves every student Welup Digital will ever train.

marketOpportunity:
Market Opportunity & Competitive Advantage:
Nigeria's digital economy is projected to contribute over $88 billion to GDP by 2030, according to the Nigerian National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy. The demand for skilled digital professionals is growing faster than the current training infrastructure can supply. This is not a future projection. It is a present reality that companies across every sector are navigating today, often unsuccessfully, because qualified local talent is simply not available in sufficient volume.

The addressable market for digital skills training in Nigeria is significant and largely underpenetrated outside of Lagos. An estimated 33 million young Nigerians between the ages of 18 and 35 are currently unemployed or underemployed, representing a generation with both the motivation and the need for credible, affordable skills training. In Edo State alone, youth unemployment significantly exceeds the national average, and access to quality training remains structurally limited.




Competitive Advantage
Focus on affordability: Cater to the needs of budget-conscious learners by offeringrelatively lower pricing, and flexible payment plans.

Personalized coaching and career support:
Differentiate by providing dedicated coaching, thriving community, mentorship opportunities and career services to ensure job readiness swiftly. 

Target under-served demographics: Fill the gap by specifically targeting mid-career professionals seeking career transitions and recent graduates/underemployed individuals.

Data-driven approach: Track and analyze user data to optimize learning outcomes and continuously improve the platform.
socialImpact:
Social and Economic Impact
Welup Digital's impact model operates on two levels: individual economic transformation, community workforce development, and state-level economic contribution.

At the individual level, every student who completes a Welup program gains access to income opportunities that were structurally unavailable to them before training. Our graduate outcomes include salaried employment in Nigerian and international companies, freelance income from global clients, and entrepreneurial ventures built on newly acquired digital competencies. For young people in Edo State, where economic opportunity has historically required physical relocation to Lagos or Abuja, this represents a fundamental change in what is possible without leaving home.

At the community level, the Welup Edo Digital Accelerator targets 700 to 1000 young people within a single grant cycle. Each employed graduate has a measurable multiplier effect on their immediate household and community through income generation, local spending, and the referral of peers into the program. A community of 500 digitally employed young people in Benin City does not just represent 500 individual success stories. It represents the beginning of a locally grounded digital talent ecosystem that Edo's private sector can recruit from and build on.

At the state level, the impact compounds across two dimensions. First, direct job creation: Welup Digital projects the creation of 500 direct and indirect jobs within the 12-month grant period, comprising new internal hires at Welup, graduate placements in employment and freelance income, and corporate training contracts that upskill existing Edo State employees. Second, talent retention: by creating credible, income-generating opportunities within Edo State, this program directly addresses the brain drain dynamic that has consistently depleted the state of its most ambitious young people.
longTermVision:
Welup Digital's long-term vision is to become the leading digital skills training institution in West Africa, with Edo State serving as the foundational proof point for a model that scales across every underserved state and country in the region.

Within three to five years, we are building toward four concrete outcomes.
A Fully Proprietary Learning Infrastructure. The LMS funded through this grant is the first phase of a broader technology vision. By year three, Welup Digital's platform will support fully asynchronous and hybrid learning delivery across multiple African markets, with automated certification, employer integration, and AI-assisted personalised learning pathways built directly into the system. The goal is a platform that can onboard and train thousands of students simultaneously with minimal proportional increase in operational cost.

A Pan-Nigerian Corporate Training Network. Our corporate training arm currently serves 50+ organisations. Within five years, the target is 500+ active corporate clients across Nigeria, with dedicated enterprise contracts in Edo State, Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, and Kano. Corporate training represents our highest-margin revenue stream and our most direct channel for employer integration at scale. Growing this arm aggressively is central to both our financial sustainability and our graduate placement outcomes.

A Regional Presence Across West Africa. Nigeria is the starting point, not the destination. The digital skills deficit that Welup Digital addresses is not unique to Nigeria. It is a West African structural problem. By year five, Welup Digital will have established training operations in at least two additional West African markets, beginning with Ghana and Rwanda, leveraging the LMS infrastructure to deliver curriculum at low marginal cost across borders.

A Self-Sustaining Scholarship Ecosystem. Within five years, Welup Digital will establish a dedicated scholarship endowment funded through a percentage of corporate training revenue, alumni contributions, and strategic partnerships with international development organisations. The target is 500 fully funded scholarships annually for young people from low-income households across Nigeria, with Edo State maintaining a permanent allocation within that pool.

The thread connecting all four outcomes is the same: technology reduces the cost of delivery, corporate partnerships sustain the revenue model, and geographic expansion multiplies the impact. Welup Digital is not building a training company. We are building the infrastructure through which Africa's next generation of digital professionals will enter the workforce.
whyInvest:
We are not coming to EYIF with an idea. We are coming with a proven model, a functioning operation, and a specific ask: help us deploy what already works into Edo State at the scale this moment demands.

That distinction matters enormously for EYIF as an investor. Capital deployed into an organisation with no operational track record is a bet. Capital deployed into Welup Digital is an acceleration. The risk profile is fundamentally different, and the probability of measurable, reportable impact within the grant cycle is significantly higher.

Here is what EYIF gets from this investment specifically.
Immediate, verifiable impact in Edo State. We already have 142 Edo students. We already have the curriculum, the employer relationships, and the operational systems. The grant does not fund a setup phase. It funds execution from day one.

A technology asset that outlasts the grant cycle. The LMS we are building does not disappear when the 12 months end. It becomes a permanent piece of infrastructure that reduces the cost of training every future Edo student Welup Digital will ever serve. EYIF's investment creates compounding returns that extend years beyond the grant period.

A credible partner for future EYIF initiatives. Welup Digital's corporate training relationships, alumni network, and employer pipeline represent assets that EYIF can leverage for future youth employment initiatives in Edo State. This is not a transactional relationship. It is the beginning of a long-term institutional partnership.

Quantifiable job creation and income generation. Within 12 months, we are projecting 1,000 direct and indirect jobs created, 7,000 Edo youth trained and transitioned into employment or freelance income, and a 5x increase in revenue demonstrating that the model scales as invested.

EYIF exists to back organisations that can transform Edo's youth employment landscape, not incrementally, but structurally. Welup Digital is that organisation. We have the proof, the plan, and the people to deliver. This grant is the catalyst that turns what we have already built into something Edo State will feel for a generation.
